title: The wedding feast
hook: a meal to celebrate, even with one sheep (Bukhari)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the mahr, the bride's gift, a free gift that belongs to her. Your line was hers alone. What did you give that was fully someone else's? Day one thousand two hundred nineteen.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf walks into Medina with a trace of yellow on his clothes, the color of a perfume, and the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ notices. What's this? I've married a woman of the Ansar, he says. The Prophet asks what he gave her. A date stone's weight of gold. And then the Prophet tells him the next thing to do. Not buy a house. Not throw a party to impress the town. In Sahih al-Bukhari, his words come down to this: hold a wedding meal, even if it's only one sheep. The marriage is made. Now feed people. Today's word: walimah.
screen: `A TRACE OF YELLOW ON HIS CLOTHES.` → `I'VE MARRIED.` → `HOLD A MEAL, EVEN WITH ONE SHEEP.`

segments.voice: Walimah is the wedding feast, the meal that celebrates and announces a marriage. Day before yesterday the nikah needed a public celebration. This is it, served on plates. First, the size. Even one sheep. The point of the instruction isn't the menu. It's that there should be a meal at all, shared, so the marriage is known and the joy is passed around. Second, what a feast can look like. In Bukhari, the companion Anas describes a wedding meal the Prophet gave with no bread and no meat at all: dates, dried yogurt and butter, spread on a leather mat. That was the walimah. People sat down and ate. Third, who's at the table. A report in Bukhari, from Abu Hurayrah, is blunt: the worst food is the food of a wedding feast where the rich are invited and the poor are left out. The walimah can be humble. What it can't be, in that report, is a party that shuts the door on the poor. Fourth, the guests' side. Bukhari also keeps the instruction that when someone is invited to a wedding feast, they should come. Showing up is part of it. The schools discuss how strong these are: whether holding a walimah is required or strongly recommended, and when a guest may excuse himself. But the shape is plain enough to fit on a leather mat. A marriage is made with words. Then it's celebrated with food, and the guest list reaches past the people who can invite you back. So the feast does two things at once. It tells the town: these two are married. And it turns a private joy into something a neighbor can taste.
screen: `EVEN ONE SHEEP.` · `DATES AND BUTTER ON A LEATHER MAT.` · `THE WORST FOOD: RICH IN, POOR OUT.` · `WHEN YOU'RE INVITED, COME.`

segments.voice: The practice: celebrate simply. Settle, and let your shoulders drop. Bring to mind the best meal you ever shared. Not the most expensive one, the best one. Who was at the table? What was actually on it? Notice how much of the memory is the food, and how much is the people. Now think of a small good thing in your life or someone else's that hasn't been celebrated. A new job, a recovery, a first week somewhere. Picture a simple table for it, and one person you'd invite who doesn't usually get invited. If you pray, you can give thanks in your own words. The bell holds the time.
Walimah. The wedding feast, held to celebrate and announce a marriage, even if it's only one sheep, with the poor at the table too. Today's word.
Your line: feed people. Today, share food with someone, even a snack or a cup of tea, and choose someone who wasn't expecting it. Day one thousand two hundred nineteen.

howItsDone: After a nikah, a Muslim family may hold a walimah, a wedding meal for relatives, friends and neighbors, which may be a simple dinner at home or a large hall reception; guests who are invited are encouraged to attend.

original.note: Arabic: a feast, and especially the wedding meal that celebrates a marriage.

trapdoor: what you thought: a walimah is the big, expensive wedding reception.
what it means: a walimah is the meal that celebrates and announces a marriage, as small as one sheep or a mat of dates.
what a scholar hears: the schools' debate over whether the walimah is required or strongly recommended, and the reports that keep the poor at the table.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 5167 (Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf: hold a wedding meal, even with one sheep)
Sahih al-Bukhari 5085 (Anas: a wedding meal with no bread or meat; dates, dried yogurt and butter on a leather mat)
Sahih al-Bukhari 5177 (Abu Hurayrah: the worst food is a wedding feast for the rich without the poor)
Sahih al-Bukhari 5173 (when invited to a wedding feast, come)

Bukhari 5167 / 2048 / 5155 (Abd al-Rahman: yellow trace of perfume, 'a date stone's weight of gold', 'hold a walimah even with one sheep'): confirm number and details.

Bukhari 5177 is Abu Hurayrah's statement; Muslim 1432 has it from the Prophet. The script says 'a report in Bukhari, from Abu Hurayrah'. Confirm.
